sentences: RDNA2 float ops return NaN, ±inf and −0 as computed, and Vulkan lets the driver assume none of them occur unless the module says otherwise.
Every module therefore declares `OpExecutionMode %main SignedZeroInfNanPreserve 32` (capability `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve`, core since SPIR-V 1.4).

Its index entry lists `"float_controls": ["shaderSignedZeroInfNanPreserveFloat32"]`, the device property it needs; `vk_pipeline_check` skips the shader where that property is false, and `--no-float-controls` leaves the mode out.
Measured on AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 26.11.2).
Without the mode, `runtime/test/shaders/cs_signed_zero_nan.asm` gets 0 in out[4..7]: the `x != x` NaN checks fold to false and a NaN `v_cvt_f16_f32` is lost.
The f16 fuzzer (`tools/valu_fuzz.py --family f16`) also saw `v_pk_mul_f16` −0 products come back +0, and, with integer f16 narrowing (#575), NaN results that were never stored.
With the mode, the test and those programs match.
Other drivers, from testers in #664: RADV (RX 7800 XT) folds the f16 NaN check (out[6]) without the mode; NVIDIA and Intel Arc keep all three either way.
Apple GPUs (MoltenVK) report the property, and the mode fixes their NaN checks, but −0 products (out[0], out[2], out[3]) still come back +0 with or without it (#1203, SHADER-182).
`check.py` and `scripts/run_gpu_tests.py` don't judge those three words on an Apple device.

Mesa's llvmpipe, where the CI runs these tests, returns 0 for the `0 × inf` NaN check (out[5]) with or without the mode, while its other NaN checks give 1 (#664), so out[5] isn't judged there (`UNJUDGED_WORDS` in `check.py`). f64 (`SignedZeroInfNanPreserve 64`) isn't declared yet.
